utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that they were documented and I knew about them from the very careful documenting of UNHCR in our office in the same headquarters at Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now at the beginning of my cross-examination I showed the multi-dimensional peacekeeping handbook. One of the things I pointed out to you was the necessity to "show the flag." And right now I'd like to show you a video-clip. It is a compilation. We don't need to play the sound, although we have disclosed the sound to the Prosecution. What is important here, Mr. Roberts, is for you to look at the background. These are three spokesmen or PIOs for the United Nations. The first person you will see is Christopher Gunness, who was the UN spokesman in Zagreb, as you know. The next person you will see is Alexander Ivanko, who is the UN spokesmen in Sarajevo, and the third person you will see is yourself. And if you could look in the background we can play the clip. We don't need to the play the sound, and for the booths, we have no need for any translation.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, that is it just one example. I could have brought a lot of video of you holding your press conferences in the Serb army of Krajina press centre under the Republika Srpska Krajina flag and map. You note what your colleagues, where and how they would hold their press conferences. I pointed out to you at the beginning the need for impartiality and its impact on a peacekeeping mission. Do you think it was appropriate for you to be holding your press conferences in the army of Serb Krajina press centre?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not think it was appropriate. At the time we had also attempted to have press conferences in the Sector South headquarters with the UN flag behind. We passed on this information to our chiefs of public information in Zagreb that they were not prepared to come or rarely would come to press briefings at the UN Sector South headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who wouldn't come?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which journalists?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists from the so-called Krajina Serb press centre and journalists who were based there from -- throughout Knin representing the various media agencies, Belgrade, Serbs from Banja Luka and Serbs from Knin who were based or working out of Knin at the time. And the advice back was twofold. I was asked for my opinion on this. I gave my opinion that what was important, I'm not sure the actual date of the clip you're showing, but I had advised very early on in my presence in Knin it was not appropriate to only talk to the press in Knin. We had to be giving the same picture, the same information, the same chance for access to journalists in Croatia. We could not bring journalists in Croatia into what was rightfully their territory, Croatia, and we established press briefings, I established press briefings with the support of our headquarters in Zagreb in Zadar. These also were held in the centre of town. Sometimes we had the UN flag; sometimes we did not. But the importance was we wanted to convey information not only to one side of this big dispute. It was that we broke out and went to the press also in Zadar and gave them in the same information from the UN in regard to the UN's actions and the mandate and the cease-fire agreement to both press sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, name, first of all, the person in the United Nations who authorised you to hold UN press conferences in the army of Serb Krajina headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it wasn't a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you who authorised it?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then public information officer, Michael Williams, chief public information officer. Before Michael it was Shannon Boyd, who is the chief of public information under Cedric Thornberry. And later Chris Gunness, who's the deputy chief spokesperson in Zagreb and Phillip Arnold, who was the chief of public information after Michael Williams. They knew about this. It was not a secret. Importance was as we saw it and as in your manual to regularly inform the public about the role and mandate and work of the United Nations. This -- sorry. This we did. It is not for any spokesperson of the UN to control how a journalist will portray what he or she says, and I'm beginning to look through this thing of the quotations that you put me in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, you can certainly control where you're holding your press conferences. You can certainly hold your press conference in Sector South. You could have them in a neutral site in town under the UN flag. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that we tried to do this in the obvious location, which is Sector South headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And because of some apparent pressure now that you're saying from the Krajina Serb authorities or journalists, you decide to move a UN public information campaign into the ARSK headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm hearing you use the words "because of some pressure."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was not a pressure. There was an issue of do we try to inform the public through the Krajina Serb press and continue to do press briefings or do we not hold them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's get to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First if I could tender the video.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is important to get to that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Tender the video 1D41-0091.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The previous one, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That I just showed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, we have no objections, but do we have dates and locations of these video-clips?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think the dates were on the -- on the videos. If it's not on the last one [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least of some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not all. Madam Registrar, the video without transcripts or translations.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D699, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D699 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, let's show Mr. Roberts 1D41-0323. This is a Security Council resolution from March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now 3 is March 1995. If we could scroll to the middle. The Security Council reaffirming its commitment to the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Republic of Croatia including its rights and obligations in respect of control over its international trade. In the last paragraph, once again, the Security Council says: "Recognizing that major provisions of the United Nations peacekeeping plan for the Republic of Croatia remain to be implemented, in particular, those regarding demilitarisation of the areas under the control of the local Serb authorities, the return of all refugees and displaced persons to their homes, and the establishment of local police forces to carry out their duties without discrimination against persons of any nationality in order to protect the human rights of all residents, and urging the parties to agree to their implementation." If we could go to page 3, please. Paragraph 5: "The Security Council decides that UNCRO shall be an interim arrangement to create the conditions that will facilitate the negotiated settlement consistent with the territorial integrity of Republic of Croatia and which guarantees the security and rights of all communities living in a particular area of the Republic of Croatia, irrespective of whether we constitute in this area a majority or a minority." Now that is the Security Council's resolution of 31 March 1995. My question to you is: Do you see any inconsistency between the Security Council reaffirming its commitment to the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Republic of Croatia and its public information officer holding press conferences in the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the resolution is very clear, and the position of myself and my senior personnel in Zagreb was that the press and the politicians in Knin be informed of that as vigorously and as often as possible. And that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How seriously --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that was the message that we had to keep --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How seriously were they going take you insisting on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Republic of Croatia at your press conferences which are sitting under the Krajina Serb flag and in the army headquarters? How seriously do you expect the Krajina Serb leadership to take you?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the job was to get across the message to the press and that was the role we had, and the press there were not just from Knin and the immediate Krajina. They were from other areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina, mainly Serbs, who would also report those stories. The position was that we continue to give press briefings to the Serb community in Knin. This was known about by the headquarters in Zagreb and I had asked for guidance certainly on more than one occasion and there had been no objection and there had also been a view that so long as that time we were advising, informing the press on both sides, both access points, to continue trying to inform the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, I'm going take you to your 1997 witness statement now, at paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if I could tender that Security Council resolution, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from Mr. Waespi. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit D700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D700 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts, at paragraph 40 of this statement, you talk about General Gotovina. In the last -- second-to-last sentence --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could that just come up --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure. It is it P675, please. Here at paragraph 40, second-to-last sentence, sorry. In the middle of the paragraph let's start there. You say: "General Gotovina, however, he turned away from the discussion and came over to say he wanted to tell me he thought the UN information I was giving was incorrect and it was keeping Serb hopes alive. He said they had heard me on the radio Korenica in the Lika area and that, inter alia, 'you're referring to this word Krajina. You should know there is no such place as Krajina. You should tell the Serbs they are in Croatia, be part of Croatia, and put away dreams of something, you are responsible for this failure.'" General Gotovina told you at that time meeting, General Gotovina was consistent with the UN handbook of what a public information officer should be doing, which is explaining to the Serb population what the UN mandate is. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting this out in my statement to show without any kind of wish to hide anything what General Gotovina said at that time to me in terms of his views, if that's what his carry correctly, then fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And he had a problem with the fact that you were not telling the Serb population and its leadership of the UN Security Council resolutions referring -- or reaffirming that this area was part of the sovereign state of the Republic of Croatia, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what he told you.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me. I am not sure that General Gotovina or Croatian authorities are aware of what I said on record as the UN spokesperson in Knin to the Serb press on many, many occasions, that this is for the UN, the Republic of Croatia, you can call it what you wish, but any final settlement has to be on the basis that this is the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are not reported for the obvious reasons that I have said before, but they were stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know what obvious reasons are, but let me ask you this. Do you think that in your dealings with General Gotovina he may have had a problem with you for, amongst other reasons, holding these conferences under the RSK flag in the RSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, an issue of that, that is for General Gotovina to express, but he didn't in the meetings that I was present at with sector commanders express that to me in terms of, You should stop doing that. And on this issue of you're referring to this word Krajina, yes, I did say on the radio station in Korenica the word Krajina not with the republic of but in terms of the region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, there also is no -- and there wasn't an administrative region of Krajina even under the Socialist Republic of Croatia. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would differ with you. I think that there is if you go back historically a geographic reference to the term Krajina as being a region. In terms of it being on both sides of the present international border of Bosnia and Herzegovina the western Krajina and the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're talking now also, sir, are we not, about Krajina in terms of this ICTY trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I refer it as Sector South. I don't use that term, but you would agree with me that that term is a historical term and not an administrative term that existed in the Socialist Republic of Croatia in 1990. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you and also say that on the most part we were advised from head office public information Zagreb that the safest way of dealing with these very strong emotive claims by the Serbs in the so-called Krajina was to use the word United Nations Sector South. And that's something we did regularly to try and avoid problems or to get the message across that there was an UN presence here and what we were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would like to turn to a different topic, Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could call up 1D41-0087.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you two documents, so I'd ask you to -- I will take you through the first one, I'll take you through the second one and then I will ask you a few questions. This is an order from Milan Martic dated 5 April 1993, is an order for the beginning of an intelligence operation called operation -- operative action Horizont. It says: "In order to gain timely information of the position, further intentions and the true function of the UNPROFOR in our territory, the operative action Horizont is being introduced." Third paragraph: "Due to previous negative experiences and the elimination of new ones, it is absolutely necessary to direct maximum operative effort the at the entire UN operations?" And in numbered paragraph 1: "Conduct complete operative verification of information for the citizens of the RSK who were in whatsoever way (interpreters, drivers, liaison officers, et cetera) connected with the UN members. Based on the verification, results such individuals should be contacted, instructed and trained with the aim of collecting quality information." "3. The members of the UNPROFOR who demonstrated a certain bias towards us and realistic view of our situation, should be instructed and conditions be created for their involvement either in monitoring the activities of the UNPROFOR or the positions of the Croatian side." Number 4: "Special focus should be drawn on the members of the civilian sector and civilian police because they have so far been the most activity (reporting to the UN base about the assessments of the current situation in the RSK, as well as proposals for undertaking further measures, intelligence activities, et cetera) and as such are of vital interest for the service." If we could go to the next page, please. Paragraph 5: "If possible, their radios and other means of communication should be controlled."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I tender this exhibit and I move on to the next one before I pose a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be Exhibit D701.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D701 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, I take it that you have carefully considered whether there was a need to read all these documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- before you put a question to the witness. We'll hear your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It will be a series of questions, some of which I won't get to today, but ... Madam Registrar, if I could now call up 1D41-0003. This is an RSK General Staff security department document, 29 May 1995, security situation in the Serbian army of the Krajina. You can look through it. There are various operative actions underway. If we could go to the next page, please. The bottom of the page in English. "In relation to the activities of the UNPROFOR and other international institutions, we are conducting five OPOs, these being the following." If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just read that from down a little bit -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] finish today, so -- finish this portion today, I mean. If you can start in the section that says OPO Prag. I will read this portion to you. It says: "The processing was introduced on 3 October 1994 aimed at monitoring the activities of the UNPROFOR members in Sector South." The next sentence says: "The focus of processing was on the Sector South commander General Kotil and the Sector South spokesmen Alun Roberts." The following methods were applied: "Work with agent, secret wire trapping and secret search of personal belongs, the activities of the persons who are objects of this processing is being monitored by than more than ten agents. The agents network is composed of mostly interpreters and a small number of administrative and assistant staff. Through the agents we managed to establish partial control of the activities of the said persons, objects of processing, to identify the main persons responsible for the intelligence work directed at the Serb army of the Krajina and to create the conditions for the application of other combined work methods of the security organ towards these institutions." Go to the paragraph that says "through mediation of the agents, a number of original written materials and documents have been seized indicating the activities, the responsible persons and connections of the UNPROFOR members in the territory of the Sector South AOR, as well as the activities, locations and strength of the HV forces in the zone of contact in the sector." Mr. Roberts, as you read this document and as you reflect back on this period, what might -- have the RSK army intelligence have been doing such that they felt that they had managed to establish partial control of your activities?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I can tell you that several of us were reasonably sure that phones were being tapped and maybe that a number of our interpretation staff should be very carefully -- I wouldn't say watched but we should be careful with certain people in terms of documentation being available and not taking them into any confidential-type meetings inside the Sector South headquarters. For the record, this is the very first time have I seen this document. I was told by local staff in Sector South that I might be subject to being monitored, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not surprised to read it, but I have no idea what it amounts to. In fact I would say, in a way, it's really a rather ambitious nonsense. I'm not trying to wipe it away, but it is in a way for me, without being dismissive, rather amateurish from the style we so often saw, I think, of the so-called RSK authorities in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Roberts, these amateurs managed to get the PIO in Sector South to conduct his press conferences in the ARSK army headquarters, so how amateurish do you think they were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that asking for a judgement or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... he used the term amateurish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, Mr. Misetic, please. Further, Mr. Roberts, could I look at C, is there -- no -- move to the next page. I do understand there is some time but are you putting to Mr. Roberts certain portions where apparently the -- the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's a lot more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but there is also -- if you have read under C, he would have also have seen, because I have an opportunity to read it, that the sympathy for the Croatian cause was apparently also on the mind of the Serbs and that's of course, part of the story as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. He can do that, but I have a lot more material to cover and then we can make the judgement on -- you know, without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- for the third time the witness saying let me see the document so I can read, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, at the same time we should be careful not put one line, not giving a witness an opportunity to look at the context and then ask some questions and that's not in every respect fair to a witness. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll tender the two documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I have, unfortunately, I have to very strictly, that's for all of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two documents you would like to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm very limited today in my time as to stop at strictly quarter to 2.00, so if you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll finish -- oh, I'll tender it tomorrow, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I do not whether these were the last two documents of your cross-examination or the last two documents of the subject for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of today, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then under those circumstances I prefer that you keep them for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
